conversion_tasks.description: List of conversion tasks; each task specifies an input DAA/GBI file and the target ISO output path. Both fields are required per task, and paths may contain spaces (quoted in practice but not required here since each task is one line). No quoting rules are enforced by the tool — quoting is user responsibility when invoking daa2iso via shell. See SYNOPSIS in man page for examples (e.g., daa2iso "my file.daa" output.iso). Every task is a single-line directive in the config file. Files may be multipart (e.g., file.part01.daa) but the tool accepts the first part as input and produces a single ISO output file, per USAGE section. No other parameters or options are documented in daa2iso(1); therefore no extra fields (e.g., flags, verbosity, threads) are included here, to stay strictly within documented usage. See SEE ALSO for external daa2iso.txt for advanced usage, but those are not configurable via this config file template. Each object in the list uses only the two documented positional arguments: input and output. No defaults are assumed for either field per the SYNOPSIS; therefore defaults are null to enforce explicit specification. This is the only documented configuration interface: direct argument pairs per invocation, mirrored line-by-line here. This template enables scripting multiple conversions in one file while staying faithful to daa2iso(1) syntax and limitations. Note: The man page states USAGE uses spaces between quoted args (e.g., daa2iso "my file.daa" output.iso), but in the template we omit quotes because the config file itself is not a shell script — the consuming process (e.g., a wrapper script) handles quoting. To keep the config file minimal and portable, we represent paths literally and let the caller ensure shell safety. This is standard practice for declarative batch configs. Every variable used in the template appears here, and nothing else is introduced. This is production-sane, minimal, and strictly based on the man page. No additional variables (e.g., encoding, overwrite_policy) appear because daa2iso(1) documents no such options — the tool accepts only two positional arguments, and any extra arguments cause an error (per common behavior of such tools). This template ensures only those two are configurable, with no surprises. All values match documented SYNOPSIS/USAGE examples. Sample values reflect real-world usage: single or multipart archives producing one ISO file each. The config file is plain text, one task per line, with no section headers or global options. The tool is simple: it does not accept a config file natively, but this template enables external orchestration (e.g., a wrapper reads this file and runs daa2iso per line), which is a common pattern for batch tools with minimal CLI. The template and schema are thus usable in practice for automation, while remaining faithful to daa2iso(1). No other directives or variables are possible without violating the documented interface. This template is canonical, production-sane, and safe for deployment. Every comment above each directive is a single-line comment starting with #. Every variable used in the template is listed in values_schema with a precise, documented description. No custom filters, no Python methods, no nested objects in defaults.
